title: Migrate a critical image loading hint with measured intent
businessContext: Review a focused Next.js application change before it reaches production. The proposed file below contains the defect or unsupported assumption; external application services, where imported, are integration boundaries.
problemStatement: Review the proposed app/hero.tsx change. Identify the incorrect framework assumption, propose a minimal corrected implementation, and provide evidence for the selected version scope and its 15/16 differences. Explain the interview variation after solving the base task. This is a framework code review: actual rendering, routing and cache behavior must be checked in a real Next.js build, not a browser function sandbox.
starterCode:
import Image from 'next/image';
export default function Hero(){return <Image src="/hero.jpg" alt="Product workspace" width={1200} height={800} priority loading="lazy"/>;}

codeReviewFiles.newCode:
import Image from 'next/image';
export default function Hero(){return <Image src="/hero.jpg" alt="Product workspace" width={1200} height={800} priority loading="lazy"/>;}

constraints: Preserve the stated user behavior and keep trust boundaries explicit.
Use the selected version’s documented API; do not suppress build/type failures to hide the defect.
Inspect the head preload and image request in a production build.
Compare LCP and bandwidth on a small viewport.
Verify below-the-fold images do not all receive the same critical hint.
candidateTasks: Add actionable line-level review comments explaining impact and correction.
Write the corrected file in the local IDE copy; split annotated companion files where instructed.
Record actual build/request/navigation evidence against the acceptance checks and compare version notes.
hints: Loading hints are a resource-priority decision, not a badge to apply to every image.
Inspect the head preload and image request in a production build.
alternativeApproaches: Avoid preloading a resource before you know it will be used. Measure which representation becomes LCP and consider fetchPriority or eager loading where the current docs recommend them.
commonMistakes: Verifying only next dev when the behavior depends on production rendering or bundling.
Treating a visible UI state, matcher or TypeScript type as a substitute for server-side validation and authorization.

verification: Inspect the head preload and image request in a production build.
Compare LCP and bandwidth on a small viewport.
Verify below-the-fold images do not all receive the same critical hint.
nextjsPractice.next15: Use the documented priority behavior for a deliberate critical image. Do not combine an intended eager critical resource with lazy loading.
nextjsPractice.next16: priority is deprecated in favor of the current loading guidance including preload. Choose preload/fetchPriority/loading deliberately and avoid competing hints.
